long_biography.plain_text:
A business partner gave Lars Windhorst a Christo drawing when he opened an office in Hong Kong in 1995. The work included a piece of fabric from the artist’s wrapping project. It became an early connection to the collection Windhorst later acquired, documenting Christo and Jeanne-Claude’s transformation of Berlin’s Reichstag.

In 2015, Windhorst bought the collection and lent it to the German parliament without charge for an initial twenty years. Drawings, models, photographs and original materials traced the project from its conception to its realisation. The arrangement brought a privately owned collection into the building it depicted, where visitors could see it on guided tours.

confidence.reason: Contemporary interview reporting and the recipient parliament document the gift, purchase, loan and public access.
